decision.detail: I cap the reel—thumb on the flange, twist, seat it—then slide it into the metal case and zip the bag shut. The Rialto booth is still warm behind me, the mic cable coiled on the floor where Rita left it. I don't go back to look. I walk the short stretch to the station, pass the ballroom where the lights are doing that slow sweep over the ceiling, and I don't slow down. At the patch I set the case down flat, open it, and rest the reel on the spool. I leave the case open so whoever picks it up sees what's inside. I pull my shoulder out of the bag strap and leave it hanging on the hook by the door. I don't turn back toward the ballroom. I don't turn back toward the Rialto. I walk out the service door, down the two concrete steps, and I'm on the street with the February air in my teeth and the bag light on my back. I'm not going home. I'm not going to the ballroom. I'm walking to the bus stop, and the bus goes past the daughter's street, and I'll stand on the corner and watch the window until it's dark in there or it isn't, and then I'll go home. The reel is on the patch. It's not in my bag anymore. It's not mine to carry tonight.
decision.intention: The reel is off my body and on the system. If the daughter calls for it, it's there. If Rita pulls it, it's there. I don't walk out of this building with it in my bag, because a bag in a bus, a bag on a kitchen table, a bag that gets left in a car—any of those is how it's gone. It's on the patch. That's a door. That's a hand other than mine. I did the one thing I could do with my hands tonight and now I'm putting them in my pockets and letting the night be a normal Tuesday night.
decision.words: I say to whoever's at the patch, not looking up: 'Rialto take. Last one on the mag. Don't let it sit past Thursday.' Then I'm gone. I don't wait for a receipt. I don't wait for a thank-you. I'm already on the steps.

messages.content: You are Larry, the camera operator. You've got one charged recording. The lights at the festival look spectacular; an old projectionist also wants to say a few words. You decide what to shoot and what to do after work. Pick an immediate physical act you can carry out, optional words and a practical intention. Your words do not make anyone else act. Silence is allowed. You may refuse, tell a lie, or leave without explaining yourself.
